scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

Imported geometry covers 1492 to 1500 across parts of Alaska. This is not a verified political boundary, beginning of settlement or extinction interval. Kodiak examples are explicitly local and are not assigned uniformly to Prince William Sound, Kenai or the Alaska Peninsula.

The museum’s live Karluk Lake page places Nikllirtuusqaq under the 1300 Years Ago section. It is not the separate 300-year-old settlement discussed higher on the page. Relative archaeological ages are retained rather than inventing exact calendar dates; none is assigned an item year.

The seven differently shaped adzes are observed objects; attribution to one carver is tentative. The engraved pebble resembles parka decoration, not an identified portrait. The burned 3000-year-old house is a separate context, and the fire’s cause is unknown in this source.

Karluk One paintings are dated using the museum’s Graphic Arts handout, printed page 39, read as indexed text and captions after the live PDF request failed. The broad 1400 to 1750 interval is approximate and does not date each artifact identically. The c.1550 box panel is the explicitly dated example.

Box and adze catalog entries were read as indexed text. The adze’s collecting date is not manufacture date. A Tlingit steaming analogy is not adopted as an Alutiiq observation. The catalog photograph does not supply an excavation layer.

The refuge account’s loss of political autonomy concerns Kodiak in 1784. No claim is made that every Alutiiq community across south-central Alaska experienced one identical conquest event. No unverified successor link is inserted.

The language-loss account contains dated historical speaker estimates, which are not repeated as current totals. Its documented 2002 start of revitalization projects and description of school punishment are used. Audio archive descriptions were read; audio was not auditioned.

The November 2024 artwork release announces planned purchases. The card says selected rather than asserting an independently verified completed accession. It identifies makers and techniques without assigning every named artist an unverified personal identity.
Independent historical review, border review and depth certification remain pending.
